question: Does the SEAFDEC-hosted LakeCon proceedings chapter expose site-resolved fish evidence for Looc Lake, and can its full text be reused?

sourceDocument.title: Fishing practices and management of fisherfolk in Looc Lake, Castillejos, Zambales
sourceDocument.publication: LakeCon2011: Building on the Pillars of Integrated Lake Basin Management (Second National Congress on Philippine Lakes)

scopeAsReportedInOfficialAbstract.studySubject: fishing practices and management of fisherfolk in Looc Lake
scopeAsReportedInOfficialAbstract.location: Barangay Looc, Castillejos, Zambales, Region III
scopeAsReportedInOfficialAbstract.historicalContext: The abstract attributes its geographic and environmental background statements to the Balaybay Agrarian Reform Community Development Plan (2004). These are source-reported historical context, not newly verified measurements or boundaries.

accessAndReuse.repositoryPageResult: Official DSpace record fetched successfully on 2026-11-24; metadata and abstract reviewed.
accessAndReuse.repositoryAccessNotice: The record states the publication remains available in print and for sale at the AQD bookstore and that the library is restricted from sending PDFs of publications still for sale.
accessAndReuse.fullText: Not acquired. No purchase, library request, login, or third-party mirror was used.
accessAndReuse.reuseDisposition: Do not reproduce chapter text, tables, figures, or images. Seek an authorized copy and review its rights before any adaptation.

evidenceDecision.decision: Record the proceedings chapter as a historical Looc Lake fishery-context lead only. Its official abstract does not expose a species list or a fish-to-station assignment. Do not infer absence from the abstract or derive a species checklist from the title or general fishery context.

limitations: The official abstract does not report survey dates, gear, sample counts, scientific names, vouchers, or species-by-site assignments.
The repository's for-sale and PDF-supply notice means the full text was not acquired; this is an access limitation, not a finding that no authorized copy exists.
The abstract's 52 ha figure and historical environmental statements are attributed background claims and are not validated lake geometry or current measurements.
No reuse license was found in the reviewed record.
This review does not establish current fish presence, fishing access, safety, legal status, abundance, catchability, diet, or bait recommendations.
nextStep: If an authorized print or library copy becomes available, review the fish taxa, field methods and dates, station assignments, specimen evidence, source lineage, and item-specific reuse terms. Until then, retain this as metadata-level historical context only. Central Luzon and Luzon remain incomplete.
